description: Single source of truth for TokenPort upstream-sync conflict resolution. Consumed by token-platform/scripts/resolve_tokenport_sync_conflicts.ps1 and by any human or AI agent following scripts/sync/upstream-conflict-agent-prompt.md. Update this file (not the scripts) when the fork's conflict surface changes.

gitConfig.note: Documentation of the repo-local settings the pipeline requires. They are applied idempotently by token-platform/scripts/sync_upstream_and_deploy.ps1 and by .github/workflows/tokenport-upstream-sync.yml; agents following the prompt template set them in step 2. Keep all four places in agreement.

resolutionRules.reason: TokenPort rebrands these documents entirely; upstream edits to them are irrelevant to the fork. Normally enforced by .gitattributes merge=ours so they never conflict; if one still conflicts, take the fork side.

Append-heavy files where the fork adds keys or providers next to upstream lines. Resolution: take the full upstream side, then re-apply the fork's delta from the merge base as a zero-context patch (git apply --unidiff-zero). If the patch does not apply, both sides changed the same lines - escalate instead of guessing.
resolutionRules.postChecks: wire_gen.go and wire.go must still compile; the dockerized backend test gate (go test -tags=unit ./...) verifies this after resolution.

resolutionRules.reason: Generated lockfiles: take the upstream side, then regenerate so any fork-side manifest change is reflected deterministically.

Every other conflict is semantic (upstream and fork changed the same logic). Never auto-resolve. The pipeline aborts the merge, writes a report plus an agent brief under token-platform/output/sync-reports/, and sends an alert. A human or an AI coding agent resolves it once following scripts/sync/upstream-conflict-agent-prompt.md; git rerere records the resolution so the next pipeline run replays it automatically.

validationGates.overlay: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/check-tokenport-overlay.ps1 (run from the fork root)
validationGates.frontend: corepack pnpm@10.28.2 install --frozen-lockfile && corepack pnpm@10.28.2 lint:check && corepack pnpm@10.28.2 typecheck && corepack pnpm@10.28.2 test:run && corepack pnpm@10.28.2 build (run in frontend/)
validationGates.backend: docker run --rm -v <fork>/backend:/src -w /src golang:1.26.5-alpine go test -tags=unit ./... (token-platform/scripts/check_tokenport_ci_parity.ps1 adds golangci-lint and pnpm-audit parity; GitHub CI additionally runs integration-tagged tests, which only run there)

invariants: Never force-push, rebase, or rewrite history on any branch.
Never commit directly to the product branch; all merges land on a sync/upstream-* branch and reach the product branch by fast-forward only.
Never delete either side's functionality to make a conflict disappear.
Never edit this policy file, .gitattributes, or CI workflows as a way to bypass a conflict.
Pushing and CI gating are done by the pipeline or the human operator, not by the resolving agent.

maintenance.markers: requiredMarkers entries are brand/feature strings that must survive resolution. Update them here when TokenPort copy or the billing feature changes; scripts read them from this file.
maintenance.extending: To auto-resolve a new recurring conflict, add its file to replay-fork-delta (append-type) or theirs-then-regenerate (generated) after two consecutive manual resolutions prove the pattern is stable.
